full.description: This is a gross pathology photograph of intestinal tissue showing multiple well-circumscribed, reddish-brown nodules. The soft tissue masses appear to be protruding from the serosal or mesenteric aspect of the bowel wall. The macroscopic appearance of these fleshy, vascular nodules is characteristic of a gastrointestinal stromal tumor or a metastatic neoplasm. A scale is visible in the lower right corner to indicate the size of the lesion.

random.description: This is a gross pathology specimen photograph showing tissue from the small intestine or mesentery. The specimen exhibits prominent, well-circumscribed, reddish-brown or hemorrhagic nodules protruding from the serosal surface. The appearance is characteristic of gastrointestinal stromal tumors, neuroendocrine tumors, or metastatic deposits within the mesenteric or bowel tissue. These lobulated, vascular masses demonstrate the typical gross appearance of a hypervascular neoplastic process affecting the intestinal tract.
